maps.for: Too many false positives: write criteria or add examples
maps.ask: Is the standard for a finding missing, or does it exist but get applied unevenly?
maps.when: A review or extraction prompt returns lots of low-value findings, or its output wobbles from run to run.
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Many low-value findings, the same way every run; the prompt uses a vague word like "thorough" or "careful"
No definition of what counts as a finding
Explicit, checkable categorical criteria: what to report and what to skip
Prompt says "be conservative", "only if confident" or "high confidence only"
Hedging is not a criterion, so precision does not improve
The team can list exactly what counts
Write the criteria down, with a small code snippet for each
Criteria are clear, but output varies in shape, format or severity run to run
Rules applied inconsistently; no demonstrated standard
2 to 4 few-shot examples that show the reasoning
The boundary is hard to describe in words; ambiguous cases
Labelled examples with the reasons behind them
Real bugs are caught only on some runs
Don't drop them by voting across runs
The generator reviews its own output and misses issues
A big change is reviewed in one pass, with uneven depth
Per-file passes plus an integration pass
maps.rule: Precision comes from explicit criteria about what to report and what to skip. If you can write the categories down, write them down; use few-shot examples for consistency and for boundaries you can't easily describe.

maps.for: Fixing one noisy review category: rewrite, pause or measure
maps.ask: This one category keeps producing false positives: what kind of fix does it need?
maps.when: One review category is mostly false positives and developers are starting to ignore the good findings too.
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: The category has only a vague instruction ("inadequate handling")
Categorical criteria written as specific, testable conditions with code samples
Criteria exist, but borderline cases get a different severity each run
2 to 4 few-shot examples showing the reasoning
The category is optional, it is noisy, and trust is collapsing
Pause or temporarily disable the category while it is rewritten
You don't know which patterns are the false positives
Add a detected_pattern field and track dismissals
"Be conservative" or "only high-confidence" was added, with no change
Self-reported confidence is used to filter findings
maps.rule: To cut false positives, define the category as specific, testable conditions with code samples. Pausing a category is only for optional checks.

maps.for: Letting the model say it is unsure instead of guessing
maps.ask: Can the model express doubt, or is it forced to commit to an answer?
maps.when: The model always commits to a value, even when the input is unclear or the value is missing.
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: The model always commits; the schema has no "unsure" option
Add a flag or an "unclear" value, plus criteria for using it
The flag exists but is used unevenly
The value is not on the document
A wrong value costs far more than a human review
Two runs agree on a wrong value
Don't use agreement as a check
maps.rule: If the model can only commit, it will guess. Add an "unsure" outcome, write criteria for using it, and route on it.

maps.for: Rules or worked examples when output is inconsistent
maps.ask: Are the rules still vague, or are they clear but the hard cases keep varying?
maps.when: You have written instructions, but the output still swings from run to run.
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Output swings everywhere; levels are adjectives or the instructions are still vague
Define each level as a checkable test: explicit criteria or a decision table
Rules are concrete, but borderline cases and ambiguous combinations still vary
Boundary not demonstrated; prose alone is not enough
2 to 4 worked examples showing the reasoning
Judgement calls, and new variants are expected
Intent hard to state as rules
2 to 4 varied worked examples with reasoning; they generalise to cases the rules don't cover
A clear rule, and its instances are a small, fixed, known set
Enumerate them, so the list is complete and checkable
JSON fails to parse, or fields are missing or the wrong type
tool_use (or --json-schema) with a tight JSON schema; this fixes structure, not judgement
Content wrong in a way code can detect
Validate and retry with the specific error
The model must flag what it cannot decide, or the category set is open-ended
Enum with "unclear" or other plus a detail field
Requirements are unknown to the author
The generator misses its own errors
maps.rule: A schema fixes shape; examples fix content. When detailed instructions stop improving consistency, show 2 to 4 worked examples with the reasoning, and enumerate only stable sets.

maps.for: Project conventions ignored: are the rules even loading?
maps.ask: Are the rules actually loaded for these files, or loaded but described poorly?
maps.when: Claude Code keeps ignoring a team convention in some files or directories.
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Convention ignored, and /memory doesn't list its file
Fix the home: project CLAUDE.md or .claude/rules/
Rules don't load for some files; the convention spans many directories
Scope: a directory CLAUDE.md is folder-bound
Rules load, but output shape varies on hard cases
2 to 4 concrete examples from the codebase
Data arrives in mixed fixed formats
Generated code has bugs a fresh eye would spot
maps.rule: First check the rules load with /memory. If they do and output still varies, add a few concrete examples covering the hard cases.

maps.for: Extraction across many document layouts: tailor, route or teach
maps.ask: Do you know the layouts in advance, and are the field descriptions already clear?
maps.when: Extraction accuracy is weak on some documents, layouts or vendors.
head: Situation
Right move
Why
rows: Field descriptions are thin; errors everywhere
Expand the descriptions or state explicit criteria
Defines what counts as the value
Descriptions detailed; a steady stream of varied or unseen layouts
2 to 4 few-shot examples chosen for structural variety, with reasoning
Schema fits and definitions exist, but hard cases vary
Shows how ambiguous cases are handled
A small, fixed set of known vendors with known quirks
One prompt covers very different document types, with contradicting guidance
Classify, then route to a type-specific prompt
Validate and retry with the error
Accuracy must be validated before automating, or errors hit only some doc types
Measure by document type and field
maps.rule: Pick few-shot examples from where the model fails, showing varied structures and how fields were found. Per-case notes grow with every case and do nothing on day one.

maps.for: Broken JSON or wrong value: what a schema does and doesn't catch
maps.ask: Is the structured output wrong in its syntax, its format, or its meaning?
maps.when: Structured output is bad and you need to know whether a stricter schema will help.
head: What you observe
Kind of error
Fix
rows: Trailing commas, bad quotes, preamble, missing fields
Tool use with a strict JSON schema (forced tool)
Value has the wrong format (bad length, letters in a number)
Valid JSON, impossible value (line 412 of a 300-line file)
Validate in code and retry with the specific error; cross-check calculated_total against stated_total
Required field filled with invented data
The model answers in prose, with no tool call
Field truly absent from the source
Don't retry; make it nullable and route to a person
maps.rule: Tool use with a strict schema stops broken JSON, not wrong values. Once it is in place, the remaining errors look correct, so check meaning in code.

maps.for: Value absent, unlisted or unreadable: which schema escape hatch
maps.ask: What does the document actually say about this field: nothing, something the list doesn't cover, or something ambiguous?
maps.when: The model invents values, or a real value doesn't fit the enum or required fields.
head: What the document says
Schema fix
Why
rows: Nothing about this field, but the schema requires it
Make it nullable or optional, and describe when to leave it empty
Required means 'produce something'; this removes pressure to fabricate
Field optional, but the model still fills it
A clear value outside a mostly fixed or growing list
Enum plus other plus a detail string
Keeps validation and records the value without coercion
A small, known, stable set of extra values
Text that can't be read with confidence, or is ambiguous between two listed options
unclear plus a detail field, or examples
Flags ambiguity instead of forcing a choice
A clear value that fits, but is mapped inconsistently or lands in the wrong field
Few-shot samples, or retry with the specific error
Validate against the system of record and retry
Value present but unreadable in the scan
maps.rule: Absent value plus required field means fabrication, so make the field nullable first. Use null when the document says nothing, other plus detail when it says something clear the list doesn't cover, and unclear when the text itself is ambiguous.

maps.for: Making the model call the right tool: tool_choice settings
maps.ask: Must the reply be a tool call, and if so, which tool exactly?
maps.when: The model replies in text when you need a tool call, picks the wrong tool, or skips a step that must run first.
head: What you need or observe
Setting or fix
Note
rows: The model may answer in text or call a tool
Must call a tool; it picks the right one when it calls, but text sometimes slips through
Fine when only one tool fits
Must call a tool; several are attached, or a specific step must run first
Names the exact tool, for example metadata before enrichment
Empty result must still be structured
Forced tool plus an empty array in the schema
The model picks the wrong tool
Better descriptions, or classify then force
Must never call a tool in some step
maps.rule: auto allows text; "any" requires some tool; forced requires that tool. If selection is right and only text slips through, use any; with several tools attached, force the one you need.

maps.for: Validation failed: retry with feedback or hand off to a person
maps.ask: Is the answer actually in the document for a retry to find?
maps.when: Validation fails and retries keep failing, or someone proposes another retry.
head: What failed
Information in source?
Right move
rows: Fields mapped wrongly, misformatted, or a sum mismatch fixed on attempt two
Retry with the specific validation errors appended
The retry message is generic ("try again")
Replace it with specifics first; blind feedback gives nothing new to act on
Value present but printed in an unusual place on some layouts
Stop retrying; nullable field and route to a person
Stop retrying; allow null, since a required field creates pressure to fill it
Model miscalculates a fact you could compute
Subtle logic or judgement errors that no tool reports
Independent review instance, if the budget allows
JSON won't parse, or output format is inconsistent
Tool use with a schema for syntax; few-shot examples for format
maps.rule: Retry with the specific errors when the fix is reachable in the source. Retries can't create missing information, so when it is absent, stop retrying and route to a person.

maps.for: Catching tidy-but-wrong values: where the check must live
maps.ask: Could the model hide this mismatch, and what outside check can catch a wrong value that looks right?
maps.when: Values are well-formed and pass the schema but are wrong, or numbers don't reconcile.
head: Situation
Right mechanism
Why
rows: The model smooths mismatches before returning
Extract stated total, calculated total and a conflict flag
Recompute in code and hold on mismatch
Stop wrong values on each document
Send only doubtful items to people
Per-field confidence, calibrated on labelled data
Learn error rates by field or document type
maps.rule: If the model can hide a mismatch, make it report one: stated total, calculated total, conflict flag. Self-reported confidence and run agreement don't measure correctness; outside records and calibrated per-field confidence do.

maps.for: Measuring which review rules produce false positives
maps.ask: Who supplies the judgement of whether a finding was wrong: developer actions, or labelled samples?
maps.when: You want per-category false-positive rates before tuning or automating a review.
head: Situation
Right mechanism
Why
rows: Need per-category rates, no human labelling
detected_pattern on each finding, with dismissals logged by ID
Uses developer clicks as the signal
Need a true precision estimate, and reviewer time is available
Stratified sample of that category first
One category is mostly false positives
Noise erodes trust in good findings
Want a second opinion on hard cases
maps.rule: To find which rules are noisy, tag each finding with its rule and record each dismissal against it. Then the rate per rule is a query.

maps.for: Batch or real-time: who is waiting, and by when
maps.ask: Is anyone blocked on the result or bound by a deadline, and does each item need a tool loop?
maps.when: You are choosing between the Message Batches API and normal synchronous requests for a workload.
head: Situation
Right choice
Why
rows: Overnight report read next morning, weekly audit, or advisory review nobody waits on
Large single-call extraction, deadline days away
A merge waits on it, and batch has no latency guarantee
Non-blocking, but a person must act within a deadline, or results are needed within hours
Real-time, in parallel if needed (for example parallel subagents)
Each item needs multi-turn tool calling
Real-time, or pre-fetch the tool data
Batch has no tool loop per request
Live traffic must keep flowing during a backfill
maps.rule: Batch saves 50% but promises nothing about time. Batch only work that nobody waits on by a deadline; non-blocking is not the same as latency-tolerant.

maps.for: Working inside batch limits: tool calls, matching results, failures
maps.ask: What can a batch request not do, and how do you tie each result back to its input?
maps.when: A batch request stops at tool_use, results come back in a different order, or some requests fail.
head: Situation
Right move
Why
rows: Results must be matched to their inputs
No need to redo the batch; keeps the 50% saving
Tool data is predictable and available beforehand
Pre-fetch it into each batch request
The model must decide what to look up as it goes
Synchronous requests with a tool loop
Batch has no multi-turn tool calling
A length problem, not a tools problem
The model answers in text instead of calling a tool
maps.rule: Batch requests can't run tool loops, and results come back in any order. Pre-fetch predictable tool data, match on custom_id, and resubmit only the failed IDs.

maps.ask: Which cost levers keep the output complete?
maps.when: You are asked to cut the cost of a Claude workload without breaking what it must cover.
head: Lever
When it fits
Watch out for
rows: No latency SLA; no multi-turn tools
Trim input to the fields the task uses
Requests carry content the task ignores
maps.rule: Batch what nobody waits for; trim what the task doesn't read. Don't skip work a requirement says to cover.

maps.for: Why a review misses bugs: self-review, dilution or unclear criteria
maps.ask: What shape are the misses, and what differs between a reviewer that finds them and one that doesn't?
maps.when: A code review (often in CI) misses bugs, gives uneven depth, or produces output the next step can't use.
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Same prompt; a fresh session finds bugs, the author session doesn't
Independent instance with no prior context or generation history
Longer or deeper thinking proposed for the same session's self-review
Still self-review: same bias, more words
Large change reviewed in one pass; uneven depth, thin in the middle
Each file looks fine, but files disagree, or feedback contradicts itself across a large PR
Every session misses the same kind of bug, or an independent reviewer misses one category
Explicit review criteria, then few-shot examples
Review hangs waiting for input in CI
Findings must become PR comments or feed the next step
maps.rule: The instance that wrote the code should not review it. Per-file passes catch local bugs, and a separate integration pass catches mismatches between files.
